scenes.title: Videos from a prompt
scenes.subtitle: How Claude makes tutorial videos with code and built-in macOS tools
scenes.narration: This whole video was made by Claude, using nothing but code and the tools already on a Mac.

scenes.heading: The pipeline

steps.label: Timing
steps.detail: real audio length sets each cue

scenes.narration: Here's the pipeline. [[next]] Claude writes a script as JSON: scenes, visuals, and narration. [[next]] The built-in say command speaks each line. [[next]] Measured audio lengths set the timing of every animation. [[next]] And Remotion renders it all to an MP4.

scenes.heading: A scene is just data
scenes.narration: Each scene is a small block like this. The type picks a layout, and next markers in the narration tell each visual exactly when to appear, so the picture stays in sync with the voice.

scenes.heading: Look, then render
scenes.narration: [[next]] Before rendering, Claude grabs a still of every scene and actually looks at them, fixing anything cramped or cluttered. [[next]] Then one command renders the final video, with subtitles.

scenes.heading: Why it stays consistent
bullets: One theme shared by every video
Scenes are data, not hand-written animation
Timing comes from the real audio
scenes.narration: [[next]] Every video shares one theme. [[next]] Scenes are data, not hand-written animation. [[next]] And timing comes from the real audio, never from guesses.
